transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

No matter how interested I am, I can’t keep my attention on job training or applications long enough to finish them, even though I really want to work on cars. I recently forgot an important intake appointment for an automotive program I'd waited months for, which made my sister—who has ADHD—urge me to get evaluated. I'm just so frustrated because I feel like I'm completely stuck.
Have you struggled with these types of attention and organization problems since childhood, specifically before you turned 12?

Yes, absolutely, it goes all the way back to elementary school. My teachers were constantly moving my seat and sending notes home because I'd blurt out answers, wander the classroom, and always lose my homework or forget instructions. I wasn't trying to misbehave or cause trouble, but I just couldn't seem to stay on track even back then.
Aside from your attention difficulties, do you currently struggle with feeling physically restless, fidgeting, or having an ongoing urge to always be on the go?

Yes, definitely—my legs are always bouncing, my feet are tapping, and I'm constantly messing with pens or keys without even realizing it. If I'm forced to sit still for too long, I get this pent-up energy where I feel like I have to get up and pace just to take the edge off. My family actually jokes that I can never just "chill" because I'm always on the move, starting multiple things at once.
Do these struggles with attention, forgetfulness, and restlessness also cause significant difficulties in other areas of your life, such as at home or in your relationships with family and friends?

Yes, it's caused a lot of tension since I had to move back in with my parents, because they constantly nag me and think I just don't care when I forget bills or chores. I also tend to interrupt and cut them off during family discussions about my plans or money, which visibly annoys them and leaves me feeling really ashamed.
Have these difficulties with attention and restlessness been present consistently throughout your life, or do they seem to come and go in phases?

They have definitely been consistent throughout my life rather than coming and going in phases. It goes all the way back to elementary school when I was always losing homework and wandering around, but it has become way more overwhelming and disruptive over the last two years as I've tried to manage adult job and financial responsibilities.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), combined presentation, represented by ICD-10 code F90.0 (Disturbance of activity and attention). The patient exhibits a persistent pattern of both inattention (difficulty sustaining attention on job training, forgetfulness regarding appointments, chores, and bills) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (fidgeting, inability to sit still, subjective restlessness, blurting out answers, and interrupting others). These symptoms have been consistently present since childhood (prior to age 12, as evidenced by school difficulties) and cause significant functional impairment across multiple settings, including home life and career development.
